source: NCERT Class X, Understanding Economic Development, Economics Ch. 1.

sections.heading: 1. Development — Different Goals
points: **Development** means different things to different people — different persons have **different developmental goals**, and what is development for one may be destruction for another.
People seek not just **higher income** but also **equal treatment, freedom, security, respect, and a pollution-free environment**.
Besides income, people value **non-material things** (quality of life, dignity).

sections.heading: 2. Income and Other Criteria
points: **National development** — different persons may have conflicting notions of a country's development; we look for measures that most people accept.
**Average (per capita) income** = total income of a country ÷ its total population; used by the **World Bank** to classify countries (rich/high-income vs low-income).
But **averages hide disparities** — two countries with the same average income can differ greatly in distribution.

sections.heading: 3. Beyond Income — Health, Education, HDI
points: Money cannot buy all goods and services needed for a good life (e.g. pollution-free environment, health).
Key **development indicators**: **Infant Mortality Rate (IMR), Literacy Rate, Net Attendance Ratio, life expectancy**.
**Human Development Index (HDI)** by **UNDP** ranks countries using **health (life expectancy), education (years of schooling) and income (per capita)**.
**BMI (Body Mass Index)** is used to check nourishment; India faces both under-nutrition and issues of public health (e.g. anaemia).

sections.heading: 4. Sustainability of Development
points: **Sustainability** — development must not deplete resources or harm the environment for future generations.
Example: **groundwater over-use** (falling water table) and **exhaustion of non-renewable resources** (crude oil) threaten sustainability.
Resources must be used carefully so that future generations can meet their needs.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Different people have different developmental goals; income is not the only goal.
Per capita/average income = total income ÷ population (World Bank criterion).
HDI (UNDP) = health + education + income; India in 'medium' human development.
Development indicators: IMR, literacy rate, net attendance ratio, life expectancy.
Sustainable development = using resources without harming future generations.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Per capita income** = total income ÷ population; used by the **World Bank**.
The **HDI** is published by the **UNDP** (uses health, education, income).
**Averages hide disparities** — same average income can mean very different distributions.
**Sustainability** concerns leaving enough resources for **future generations**.
